from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Language of Vectors", 
                          ["A basis defines our coordinate system.", 
                           "Vectors are displacements, not just numbers.", 
                           "Coordinates depend on the basis chosen."])
        
        # Define base objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 3], y_range=[-2, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        i_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(1, 0), color=WHITE, buff=0)
        j_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(0, 1), color=WHITE, buff=0)
        i_label = MathTex("i", color=WHITE).next_to(i_vec.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        j_label = MathTex("j", color=WHITE).next_to(j_vec.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        basis = VGroup(axes, i_vec, j_vec, i_label, j_label)

        v_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(2, 1.5), color=YELLOW, buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex("v", color=YELLOW).next_to(v_vec.get_end(), UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_in_area(basis, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(basis), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_vec), Write(v_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        coord_label = MathTex("(2, 1.5)", color=YELLOW).next_to(v_label, RIGHT)
        self.play(Write(coord_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Problem: Viewing Space from Different Angles", 
                          ["View the same vector from different angles.", 
                           "Basis B and Basis C are perspectives.", 
                           "We need a bridge between these views."])

        self.add(basis_b, basis_c)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Express new basis vectors as old ones.",
            "These become columns of matrix P.",
            "P maps new coordinates to standard.",
            "Grid lines warp to the new basis.",
            "Now we have our transition machine."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Constructing the Transition Matrix", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Grid/Plane
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3})
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        basis_v1 = np.array([1, 1])
        basis_v2 = np.array([-1, 1])
        
        # Matrix P notation
        matrix_p = MathTex(
            r"P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}",
            font_size=36
        )
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, 'D2', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Indicate(matrix_p))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Warp effect: transform grid using linear map
        new_plane = plane.copy().apply_matrix([[1, -1], [1, 1]])
        self.play(Transform(plane, new_plane))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The formula is [v]B = P * [v]C.",
            "P translates coordinates between systems.",
            "P inverse reverses the translation.",
            "Use robots to navigate local frames.",
            "Map local movement to global space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Change of Basis Formula: The Transformation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for lecture lines
        colors = [YELLOW, BLUE, RED, GREEN, PURPLE]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        eq = MathTex("[v]_B = P \cdot [v]_C").set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(eq))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        p_label = Text("P (Translator)", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(p_label, 'C4')
        self.play(FadeIn(p_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        inv_p = MathTex("P^{-1}").set_color(RED)
        self.place_at_grid(inv_p, 'D4')
        self.play(FadeIn(inv_p))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(colors[3])
        robot = Circle(radius=0.3, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, 'E3')
        self.play(Create(robot))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(colors[4])
        path = Arrow(self.grid['E3'], self.grid['B3'], buff=0.2, color=PURPLE)
        self.play(Create(path))
        self.play(Indicate(eq))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application", [
            "We only change our coordinate description.",
            "The vector remains physically unchanged.",
            "Grid lines rotate, labels update accordingly."
        ])
        
        # Recapping Basis Formula
        formula = MathTex(r"[\mathbf{v}]_B = P^{-1} [\mathbf{v}]_A", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # 2D Grid Representation for Rotation
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3})
        vec = Vector([1, 1], color=BLUE)
        grp = VGroup(plane, vec)
        self.place_in_area(grp, 'C2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(grp))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Rotate(plane, angle=PI/6), Rotate(vec, angle=PI/6))
        self.wait(2)
        
        final_text = Text("Perspective changes.", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, 'F3')
        self.play(FadeIn(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Language of Vectors
sections.content: Briefly define a basis as a 'coordinate system' (the grid lines of a vector space). Emphasize that a vector is just a physical displacement, while coordinates are our instructions on how to reach it using basis vectors.
sections.example: Imagine a vector pointing to a treasure chest. Whether you describe its position using North/East or a rotated 'Map Grid', the treasure chest doesn't move—only the numbers (coordinates) change.

sections.title: The Problem: Viewing Space from Different Angles
sections.content: Introduce two different basis sets, B (standard) and C (the 'new' perspective). Explain that a vector 'v' can be represented as [v]B or [v]C. The goal is to find the 'bridge' (Transition Matrix) that maps coordinates from one view to the other.
sections.example: A cat (the vector) sits on a floor. Camera A (Basis B) sees it at (2, 1). Camera B (Basis C), mounted at a 45-degree angle, sees the same cat at different coordinate values.

sections.title: Constructing the Transition Matrix
sections.content: Show the visual process of expressing the 'new' basis vectors as linear combinations of the 'old' basis vectors. These coefficients become the columns of the Transition Matrix P. Visual: Use an animation of grid lines warping from a square to a tilted parallelogram.
sections.example: If your new basis vectors are v1=(1,1) and v2=(-1,1), place these as columns in matrix P to create the machine that transforms 'New Coordinates' into 'Standard Coordinates'.

sections.title: The Change of Basis Formula: The Transformation
sections.content: Formalize the equation: [v]B = P * [v]C. Explain that P is the 'translator'. To go back, we use P-inverse. Visual: A 'Translator Engine' icon where inputting coordinates from Basis C and multiplying by matrix P yields the coordinates in Basis B.
sections.example: Use a robot character navigating a room. It calculates its movement in its 'local' body-centered frame (Basis C) and uses the Transition Matrix to translate that into the 'global' room coordinates (Basis B).

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Reiterate that we aren't changing the vector, just our 'description' of it. Final visual: A side-by-side comparison of the same vector shifting its coordinate labels as the grid underlying it rotates.
sections.example: Computer graphics: Rotating a 3D model involves changing the basis of the object's vertices so they align with the camera's perspective.
